text: To do something assiduously is to do it with steady, careful, never-give-up effort. Here it says Rwanda patiently and persistently won over the European ministers, which shows how much it wanted the deal.
To burnish metal is to rub it until it shines. A burnished reputation is one polished until it looks better than before. Here it describes Rwanda hoping to be seen as a trustworthy partner.
Reticence is a holding back, a reluctance to speak openly or commit. Here it means Europeans seem quietly cautious about being too closely linked with Rwanda's government.
A paradigm shift is a basic change in the way people think about or approach a problem. The politicians use it boastfully, claiming the deal changes the whole approach to asylum.

A game-changer is something that alters a situation so completely that the old rules no longer apply. The politicians use it to hype the deal, and the article notes the officials were not exactly modest.
A milestone was originally a stone marking distance along a road; now it means an important stage reached in a project. Here an official calls the deal a big step forward.
Asylum is protection a country gives to someone who says they would be in danger if they went home. An asylum-seeker is a person asking for it; if the claim is rejected, they are expected to leave.

Asylum-seekers are people who have arrived in a country and asked for protection but whose claims have not yet been accepted. In this article they are ones whose requests have already been turned down.
A prime mover is the person or group that gets something started and pushes it forward. Denmark's prime minister is described as a leading force behind the scheme.
In this article a bid is an attempt or request, here an application for asylum. It is a sense of the word that differs from its use in auctions, where a bid is an offer of money.
A return hub is a centre in a third country that takes in migrants who have been refused asylum in Europe but cannot easily be sent to their own countries. Rwanda would host the first one.
To integrate is to become a full part of a community, for instance by learning the language, finding work and making friends. Here Rwanda's minister says migrants could settle into local life.
Bilateral means between two sides. Rwanda would sign a separate agreement with each of the five European governments, rather than one shared agreement with all of them.
A turnaround is a sudden reversal of direction. The article uses it for Europe's shift from very high migration to tighter control, with fewer irregular arrivals.
Irregular migration means entering a country without the official permission or paperwork, such as crossing a border outside the proper routes. Many governments prefer this term to some other labels.
To plummet is to fall steeply and fast, like a stone dropping. The article says irregular arrivals have fallen sharply, as the chart shows.
The asylum pact is a package of EU rules, in effect since June, that sets how member states handle asylum claims and share responsibility. The article says it may help further reduce arrivals.
To deport someone is to force a foreigner to leave a country and be sent back. The article stresses that this is hard in practice.
A return order is an official legal instruction telling a person whose claim failed that they must leave. The article says the EU issues far more of them than it actually carries out.
To fall into the shadows means to disappear from the authorities' view, living and working without official records. Here it describes rejected migrants who stay but cannot be found.

A populist politician claims to speak for ordinary people against elites, often with simple, forceful promises. Here populist-right politicians demand more extreme policies than mainstream parties do.

Remigration is a term used by far-right groups for pushing large numbers of migrants, sometimes even citizens of immigrant background, to leave. The article contrasts it with the mainstream, more orderly approach.
Safeguards are protections built into a rule to prevent harm. The EU law on return hubs includes human-rights and monitoring safeguards, which officials say make it more legally secure.
Sounder here means more solid and reliable. Officials say the new law puts return hubs on firmer legal ground than earlier schemes.
Ill-fated means doomed to fail or end badly. Britain's 2022 Rwanda plan was abandoned after costing taxpayers £715m.
Scant means barely enough or very little. Details of the plan are scant, so many questions are unanswered.
To make a dent is to have a small but visible effect, as in the surface of a car. Here the few hundred people sent will not noticeably reduce the huge number awaiting removal.
To be served with a document is to have it formally delivered to you, as with a legal order. Germany has over 250,000 people who have received return orders.
A deterrent is something meant to put people off doing something by making the consequences look bad. The British official doubts that the scheme deters anyone.
Credible means believable or convincing. Britain's plan had a stronger claim to deterrence because it would have affected more people.
Refoulement, a French word, is forcing a person to go back to a place where they would face danger. International law bans it, and critics fear it could happen to migrants in Rwanda.
A repressive government restricts freedom and punishes criticism, often through force. Critics use the word about Rwanda's government.
A do-gooder is someone whose well-meaning efforts seem unrealistic to others. Officials use it dismissively of critics, whom they see as ignoring practical limits.

Liechtenstein is a tiny, wealthy country in the Alps between Switzerland and Austria. The official's sarcastic point is that critics would object to almost any location short of a hub in a rich European country like this, so Europe will run out of options.
Vulnerable refugees are those at special risk, such as children, the sick or victims of abuse. Rwanda already hosts EU-funded centres for such people evacuated from Libya.
A militia is an armed group that is not part of a country's official army. Rwanda is accused of backing one in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Dissidents are people who publicly oppose their government, often at great personal risk. The article says Rwanda persecutes them.
Paul Kagame is Rwanda's president and has led the country since the late 1990s. He is praised for rebuilding Rwanda after the 1994 genocide and criticised for silencing opponents.
Rwanda is a small, densely populated country in East Africa, known for rapid development under President Kagame and for a tough human-rights record. Here it would host the return hub.
The Democratic Republic of Congo is a huge country in central Africa next to Rwanda, where armed groups have fought for years. Germany cancelled talks with Rwanda over its actions there.
Envoys are diplomats sent to represent their governments abroad. The article says those in the region sense that Europeans are hesitating.
Bruised here means hurt in feelings or reputation, not physically. The quote says Rwanda was stung by Britain abandoning its deal and so wants this one to succeed.
The Social Democrats are Germany's centre-left party, the junior partner in the governing coalition. The article says some of them have doubts about the plan.
Sceptical, the British spelling of skeptical, means doubtful about whether something is true or will work. France and Spain have not signed on to the plan.
To clamour is to demand something loudly and insistently. Italy and others are eager to join the return-hub plan.
An exclave is a piece of a country separated from the main territory and surrounded by another country. Ceuta is Spanish land on the coast of Morocco.
Frontex is the European Union's border and coast guard agency. It helps countries guard external borders and may be given a bigger role in deportations.
To externalise a process is to move it outside your own borders or organisation. Some governments hope to handle the whole asylum process abroad, outside Europe.
To see off a rival or threat is to defeat it or drive it away. The official says centrist politicians must act now to stop right-wing populists from winning.
